text:
erin: quick one — hitting mypy/pyright errors from the python SDK's autogenerated types for streaming chat. minimal repro below, but the generator return type is too loose and our sample app breaks.

erin: code:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
from typing import AsyncIterator

client = RedwoodClient()

async def run():
    async for chunk in client.chat.stream(model="x-large", input="hi"):
        # expecting chunk to be a ChatStreamChunk typed model
        print(chunk.delta.text)
```
erin: mypy error: "Item \"Any\" of \"AsyncIterator[Any]\" has no attribute \"delta\"" — the autogen typing is `AsyncIterator[Any]` (or `AsyncIterator[dict]`) instead of a generated ChatStreamChunk.

mike: can you paste the exact generated model type in `sdk/models/chat.py`? might be missing the streaming-specific model. :eyes:

erin: paste: `def stream(...) -> AsyncIterator[Dict[str, Any]]:` — that's the problem. we used a very generic fallback in autogen for streaming endpoints.

jia: ugh, that explains the sample app fail. quick workaround: cast the iterator when consuming it, e.g. `from typing import cast; async for chunk in cast(AsyncIterator[ChatStreamChunk], client.chat.stream(...)):` — not great but unblocks people.

oliver: long-term fixes: 1) generate explicit ChatStreamChunk dataclass/pydantic model and type the generator as `AsyncIterator[ChatStreamChunk]`; 2) emit .pyi stubs for the generated package so type checkers pick them up; 3) ensure `from __future__ import annotations` is present to avoid forward-ref noise.

mike: agree. also ran into pyright complaining about `AsyncIterator[Union[ChatStreamChunk, FinalEvent]]` vs `AsyncIterator[ChatStreamChunk]` when we emit sentinel end-of-stream objects. need to standardize: prefer a single chunk model with optional fields (e.g., `is_final: bool`) so type unions don't blow up checkers.

erin: another gotcha — our sample app pins python 3.8 for compatibility, but some of the typing (ParamSpec, Concatenate) only behave well in 3.9+. pyright users see weird errors. anyone okay with bumping min python to 3.9 for the SDK?

jia: product teams still have 3.8 infra in a couple places. can't force a bump yet. alternative: generate simpler typing that avoids ParamSpec and use runtime checks guarded by TYPE_CHECKING.

oliver: PR idea: generate a tiny `types.pyi` that exports high-level types (ChatStreamChunk, ChatResponse, Client) and keep runtime code simple. That will make both mypy and pyright happy without breaking 3.8 runtime.

mike: I'll volunteer to prototype the .pyi generator. quick plan: parse the autogen model schema, emit dataclass-like signatures, and include them in sdist/wheel under `redwood_sdk-stubs` package.

erin: ci-bot: there was a CI failure when i pushed a repro branch — log snippet: `mypy redwood_sdk tests/streaming_sample.py: error: "Dict[str, Any]" has no attribute "delta"` — so tests will catch this once we add type stubs.

ci-bot: <ci> build #4521 failed on tests/streaming-typing-repro (see https://ci/internal/4521)</ci>

jia: small UX request too: please add an example in docs showing how to type the consumer today (casting vs wrapper) so customers don't get blocked while we fix generator.

oliver: noted. I'll add a devex doc snippet + sample app change. also will open an RFC to pick the canonical shape (union vs optional final field).

mike: thanks — i'll put up a draft PR for .pyi generation by EOD. erin, can you attach your minimal repro file to the issue so i can run it locally?

erin: done, attached repro gist in the issue. moving this to a short RFC thread — thanks all. :thumbsup:
